profile.name: Aster DM Quality Care Ltd (formerly Aster DM Healthcare Ltd; renamed w.e.f. 3-Jul-2026)
profile.founded: 1987: Dr Azad Moopen opens a one-doctor clinic in Dubai; India entry 2001 (MIMS Kozhikode stake), Aster Medcity Kochi 2014
profile.listing: IPO Feb-2018 at Rs190 (NSE: ASTERDM, BSE: 540975)
profile.today: India-only hospital chain after the Gulf (GCC) business was sold in Apr-2024 and Quality Care India Ltd (CARE Hospitals, KIMSHEALTH, Evercare Bangladesh) merged in on 1-Jul-2026: 39 hospitals (incl. 4 asset-light O&M hospitals and 2 in Bangladesh), 10,898 capacity and 10,559 operational beds, 28 cities, 9 states, ~7,400 doctors, ~37,700 staff, 321 labs and patient experience centres, 205 Aster-branded pharmacies run by an associate
profile.brands: Aster (Aster Medcity, Aster CMI, Aster MIMS, Aster Ramesh), CARE Hospitals, KIMSHEALTH, Evercare
profile.src: Q1FY27 presentation pp.3-5 (5-Aug-2026); Q1FY27 call; AR FY26

merger.structure: Step 1 (share swap): Aster bought 5.0% of QCIL (1,90,46,028 shares at Rs445.83) from BCP (Blackstone) and TPG, paying with 1,86,07,969 new Aster shares at Rs456.33 (46,51,992 to TPG, 1,39,55,977 to BCP); completed in FY26 (share capital 49.95 -> 51.81 cr shares). Step 2: QCIL amalgamated into Aster by a scheme at 977 Aster shares for every 1,000 QCIL shares.
merger.terms: Issue price Rs456.33 = SEBI ICDR pricing (higher of 90- and 10-day VWAP to 28-Nov-2024); QCIL value Rs445.83 a share. Equity values used: Aster Rs22,794 cr, QCIL Rs16,983 cr; inter-se split 57.3% Aster holders / 42.7% QCIL holders. The deal valued Aster at 36.6x FY24 adjusted post-Ind AS EV/EBITDA and QCIL at 25.2x. No cash consideration ('cash neutral'). Expected post-merger holding: Aster promoters 24.0%, Blackstone (BCP Asia II Topco IV) 30.7%, Aster public 33.3%, other QCIL holders 12.0%. Aster promoters and Blackstone are joint promoters with 3 board nominees each; independent directors at least half the board; BCP's rights fall away below 10%, the Moopen family's below 5%.
merger.valuers: PwC Business Consulting (Aster) and D and P India Advisory (QCIL), reports dated 29-Nov-2024: DCF 50% and EV/EBITDA comparables (33.7x peer median for Aster, 27.8x for QCIL) / market price 25-50%; fairness opinion ICICI Securities. Discount rates 11.5% (Aster) and 12.5% (QCIL).
merger.approvals: CCI approval 15-Apr-2025; NSE/BSE no-objection 6-Oct-2025; NCLT application 11-Dec-2025; NCLT order convening meetings 21-Jan-2026; shareholders approved 10-Mar-2026 with 96.68% of votes in favour; NCLT Hyderabad sanctioned the scheme 19-Jun-2026; record date 9-Jul-2026.
merger.completion: Effective 1-Jul-2026; renamed Aster DM Quality Care Ltd w.e.f. 3-Jul-2026; 35,35,51,410 new shares allotted to QCIL holders on 13-Jul-2026; paid-up capital 87,16,72,439 shares (Rs871.67 cr).
merger.accounting: Pooling of interests under Ind AS 103 (scheme clause 17.1): QCIL's assets and liabilities are combined at book value, so no large new goodwill and book equity rises only by QCIL's book equity.
merger.costs: Merger-related exceptional costs Rs114.4 cr in Q1FY27 (Q1FY26 Rs4.4 cr); FY26 exceptional expenses Rs71.1 cr included merger costs and CSR on the GCC sale.
merger.synergies: 10-15% of FY24 pro-forma EBITDA, i.e. Rs150-200 cr, from procurement, clinical talent and programmes, IT, indirect costs, capex efficiency and medical value travel; management says none were in the Q1FY27 numbers and they start in FY27, more meaningfully from FY28.
merger.postDealSales: 19-Aug-2026: TPG's Centella Mauritius sold ~6.66% at an average Rs766.17 (Rs4,451 cr block); 2-Sep-2026: promoter entity Union (Mauritius) Holdings bought 46,09,800 shares (0.52%) at Rs760 (Rs350 cr).
merger.src: June-2026 investor presentation pp.9-14 (3-Jun-2026); scheme notice to shareholders (4-Feb-2026) pp.2-4, 28-35, 43-50; Q4FY26 presentation p.9; Q1FY27 presentation p.4; Arthneeti / InvestyWise summaries of BSE filings (25-Jun, 13-Jul, 18-21-Aug-2026); Business Today (19-Aug-2026); Sahi / BSE (2-Sep-2026)

gccSeparation.what: Affinity Holdings (Mauritius, 100% subsidiary) sold the Gulf business (Aster DM Healthcare FZC: hospitals, clinics, pharmacies in the UAE, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan) to Alpha GCC Holdings (now Aster GCC Holdings), owned 65% by a Fajr Capital-led consortium and 35% by the Moopen family.
gccSeparation.dates: Board approval 28-Nov-2023; completed 3-Apr-2024; sale consideration received Rs7,568.46 cr (AR FY26 note 10).
gccSeparation.dividend: Special dividend Rs118 a share declared 12-Apr-2024 (record date 23-Apr-2024), ~Rs5,894 cr; Aster kept ~Rs1,500 cr. FY25 dividends paid Rs6,175 cr (Screener).
gccSeparation.impactOnNumbers: Screener's FY15-FY22 history includes the GCC business (FY22 revenue Rs10,253 cr); FY23 onward is India only (restated). FY25 profit includes a Rs4,981 cr post-tax gain on the sale (Rs5,378 cr attributable profit, EPS Rs107.66). FY24 balance sheet shows the GCC as held for sale. So per-share and multiple history before FY25 does not describe today's company.
gccSeparation.src: Business Standard / Upstox (12-15 Apr 2024); AR FY26 notes 6, 10; Screener

pipelineSummary: Combined plan (Q1FY27 deck p.17): +4,179 beds to 15,077 capacity: FY27 634, FY28 1,190, FY29 1,555, FY30+ 800; 53% brownfield. Earlier (Q4FY26 deck): +4,445 to 15,068 (878 / 1,305 / 1,462 / 800). Aster alone: +2,728 beds to 8,177 (688 / 760 / 480 / 800; 964 brownfield, 1,764 greenfield).
capexPlan: Aster: ~2,500 beds for ~Rs2,700 cr over four years, Rs350 cr spent to Mar-26 (Group CFO, 1-May-2026). QCIL: ~Rs2,000 cr for ~1,700 beds in 3-4 years (Rs1-1.1 cr a bed; greenfield ~Rs1.5 cr, brownfield Rs0.8-1.0 cr) plus ~5% of revenue a year of maintenance (3% refresh, 2% new programmes) (Varun Khanna, 1-May-2026). Aster capex FY26 Rs549 cr (45% expansion); FY24-26 ~Rs1,280 cr.

governance.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells (Aster statutory auditor per the scheme certificates); QCIL audited by Price Waterhouse
governance.control: Joint control by the Moopen family (~24%) and Blackstone (~31%) under a shareholders' framework written into the articles: three nominees each, reserved matters (equity issues, new businesses, debt above 2.5x net debt/EBITDA, M&A, asset sales above Rs25-50 cr, capex above budget).
governance.relatedParty: The Aster brand is shared with the Gulf business, 35% owned by the Moopen family (brand licensing fee Rs2.3 cr a year). The Aster pharmacies are run by Alfaone Retail Pharmacies, a ~49% associate that loses money (Aster's share of associates' losses Rs37 cr in FY26) and gets a support letter from Aster. T.J. Wilson is paid by Affinity (Mauritius).
governance.pledge: TPG's Centella Mauritius pledged 8.44 cr shares (~9.7%) to lenders (disclosed 17-21 Aug-2026), then sold ~6.66% on 19-Aug-2026. We found no pledge by the Moopen family or Blackstone.
governance.src: Scheme notice (Feb-2026) pp.43-47; AR FY26 related-party and associate notes; InvestyWise (20-21 Aug-2026)

accounting.basis: Ind AS, consolidated. FY26 and earlier = Aster alone (India only from FY23 restated). From Q2FY27 the accounts include QCIL (pooling of interests, from 1-Jul-2026). Company 'operating EBITDA' excludes ESOP cost, variable O&M fees on asset-light hospitals and one-offs; Screener's operating profit is closer to reported post-Ind AS EBITDA.
accounting.leases: Lease liabilities Rs1,518 cr (Aster, Mar-26) + ~Rs267 cr (QCIL, Sep-25): asset-light O&M and leased hospitals. Post-Ind AS EBITDA (Rs901 cr) vs pre-Ind AS (Rs788 cr) for Aster in FY26: rent of ~Rs113 cr sits in depreciation and interest.
accounting.exceptionals: FY25: Rs4,981 cr gain on the GCC sale. FY26: exceptional income Rs38.4 cr (minimum-wage reversal) and expenses Rs71.1 cr (merger costs, CSR on the GCC gain, provisions). Q1FY27: Rs114.4 cr merger costs.
accounting.ccps: Rs374.38 cr equity component of compulsorily convertible preference shares sits in other equity (AR FY26) but Screener shows it as borrowings.
accounting.minorities: Aster's minorities Rs258 cr (book), Rs39 cr of FY26 profit; QCIL's minorities Rs1,518 cr (FY24 book; KIMSHEALTH founder 15-20%).
